clue.text: Opera in which Master O'Hara meets trouble head to head

indicators.note: the boy's name is turned round so that its head touches the head of the next piece

parts.note: Kim, hero of Kipling's novel, is Kimball O'Hara, a young master
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A theatre note: a boy called O'Hara runs headlong into difficulty during an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head to head' reverses KIM to MIK so its first letter meets the first letter of ADO. Kipling's Kim is Kimball O'Hara.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera set in Japan is named after its emperor.

clue.text: Mat and Mollie get round tablet

indicators.note: to mat is to tangle or snarl, so the following letters are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: Two people, Mat and Mollie, manage to circle a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mat' looks like a name beside Mollie, but as a verb (tangle) it is the anagram signal for AND MOLLIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A medallion is a large disc-shaped medal or plaque, a flat circular piece.

clue.text: Family doctor at home is a most important man

parts.note: kin means family, relatives
GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor
in means at home

explanation.surface: A family doctor who stays at home is the key figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingpin is the chief person in an organisation, the indispensable figure.

clue.text: Surprisingly, he's trained to lower spirits

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Unexpectedly, the fellow has been taught how to be gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten someone is to dampen their morale and make them lose hope.

clue.text: Mary's subject not bound to be unscathed

parts.note: Mary Queen of Scots ruled Scotland, so her subject is a Scot
free means unbound, not tied

explanation.surface: A subject of Queen Mary goes unshackled and unharmed.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off scot-free is to escape without punishment or injury.

clue.text: Victor William

explanation.surface: A two-word note pairing a winner with a king's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A conqueror is a victor; William the Conqueror took England in 1066.

clue.text: 8 day, perhaps

explanation.surface: A cross-reference: the foe from another clue, and a day as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 refers to 8 down, ENEMY: 'time is the enemy' is proverbial, and 'how goes the enemy?' asks the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial foe of us all is the passing hour; a day is one unit of the clock and calendar.

clue.text: Men in line were first to have caused irritation

parts.note: a rank is a line of soldiers standing side by side
led means were in front, came first

explanation.surface: Soldiers in formation who led the way have been annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankled festered and annoyed, leaving a lasting grievance.

clue.text: In Arden "No — But winter and rough weather"

definitions.text: In Arden "No — But winter and rough weather"

parts.words: In Arden "No — But winter and rough weather"
parts.note: a fill-in-the-gap quotation: the song in As You Like It, set in the Forest of Arden, says here shall he see no foe but winter and rough weather

explanation.surface: A line quoted from Shakespeare's forest song with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The song 'Under the greenwood tree' in As You Like It runs 'Here shall he see / No enemy / But winter and rough weather'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in the song is the foe or adversary who is absent from the forest.

clue.text: Old story the young lady lisped

indicators.note: a lisp turns an S sound into TH, so the young lady's title is said with that impediment

parts.note: Miss is the title for a young lady

explanation.surface: A girl with a speech impediment tells an ancient tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Said with a lisp, MISS comes out as 'mith'.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth is a traditional tale from long ago, often of gods or heroes.

clue.text: Chain of command

parts.note: read as a chain or succession of rulers handing down command through a family

explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty is a line of hereditary rulers, one following another.

clue.text: Sap! In one moving letter he's proposed

indicators.note: in places the word for sap inside the other piece
one letter of the word one is moved to a new position

parts.note: to sap is to undermine, to mine

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a fool, then a note about a moving letter and a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sap!' reads as an insult hurled at a fool, but it is the verb meaning undermine. 'moving letter' shifts one letter of 'one', and 'In' puts the sap word inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a person put forward as a candidate for a post or award.

clue.text: Brownie's untidy — clean her up

indicators.note: untidy says the letters are left in a messy, disordered state

explanation.surface: A Brownie Guide has made a mess, so someone must tidy her up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brownie' suggests a junior Girl Guide, but it is the household sprite of folklore; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownie is a helpful elf of folklore; the Irish fairy cobbler is another little sprite.

clue.text: Gambling, hand over about a pound

indicators.note: about means going around, so the payment surrounds the pound

parts.note: to pay is to hand over money
L, from Latin libra, stands for a pound

explanation.surface: A gambler pays out about a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Play means gambling, as in being at play at the tables.

clue.text: Lords and ladies take nuts with beer perhaps

parts.note: cuckoo is slang for crazy, nuts
a pint is a typical measure of beer

explanation.surface: Aristocrats grab nuts with their beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lords and ladies' looks like the aristocracy but is the folk name of a wild arum plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lords-and-ladies is the country name of the wild arum, a woodland plant.

clue.text: Pubs on both sides of a road to the works

indicators.note: the pubs stand either side, flanking the other pieces

parts.note: inns are pubs

explanation.surface: Inns stand on either side of the road leading to the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the works' suggests a factory but means the insides, as of a machine or body.
explanation.definitionFit: Innards are the internal parts or mechanism, the guts of something.

clue.text: Just one garment being worn

parts.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest, a garment
on means being worn, as clothes are

explanation.surface: Only a single item of clothing is being worn.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is a lone individual, one by itself.

clue.text: Fuller or, possibly, lower

indicators.note: possibly says the two letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: under means lower, beneath

explanation.surface: A remark comparing sizes: plumper, or perhaps lower down.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounder means plumper, more full in shape.

clue.text: Pick-me-up for overtime in court

explanation.surface: A tonic needed for a long day in the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: In English law a refresher is an extra fee paid to a barrister when a case runs beyond its first day.
explanation.definitionFit: A refreshing drink revives you; a barrister's daily supplementary fee pays for extra time on a long case.

clue.text: Girl eager for such material

parts.note: Nan is a girl's name
keen means eager

explanation.surface: A girl is keen to get hold of this fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally made in Nanjing.

clue.text: A breath-taking feature

parts.note: read literally, a facial feature that takes in breath rather than a stunning sight

explanation.definitionFit: Air is drawn in through the openings of the nose.

clue.text: Bad character not on commission

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man, a bad lot
off is the opposite of on

explanation.surface: A villain is not working on commission.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake-off is a share of the profits, often illicit, taken as a cut.

clue.text: The Antipodean sticks

parts.note: the sticks means remote countryside; the Australian version of it

explanation.definitionFit: The remote, sparsely settled interior of Australia is its back country.

clue.text: Long kind of bone

explanation.surface: A remark about a lengthy sort of skeleton part.
explanation.definitionFit: To long is to yearn; a forked chicken bone is pulled to make a yearning come true.

clue.text: Thin slice of iron used in conflict

indicators.note: used in puts the iron symbol inside the word for conflict

parts.note: war is armed conflict
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A thin piece of metal is employed in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A wafer is a very thin crisp biscuit or slice of anything.

clue.text: Little creature made of coloured glass?

parts.note: blue is a colour
a bottle is a glass container

explanation.surface: A small animal ornament fashioned from tinted glass.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the pun: a blue bottle would be coloured glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluebottle is a large buzzing blowfly, a small insect.

clue.text: We're thrown into jug

indicators.note: thrown suggests pottery on a wheel and here means the letters are tossed about

explanation.surface: We've been tossed into prison, as in jug slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' can be slang for prison, but it is the definition: a pitcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large pitcher, a jug with a wide mouth.

clue.text: Each dropping a point in a high degree

indicators.note: dropping says a letter falls away from the word for each

parts.note: every means each
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Everyone losing a point to a great extent.
explanation.definitionFit: Very means extremely, to a great extent.

clue.text: Give up well filled with fish

indicators.note: filled with means the word for well contains the fish

parts.note: fit means well, healthy
the orfe is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A well is stocked with fish, which must be surrendered.
explanation.definitionFit: To forfeit something is to lose or surrender it as a penalty.

clue.text: The last thing you'd say about anyone

definitions.text: The last thing you'd say about anyone

parts.words: The last thing you'd say about anyone
parts.note: read literally, the final words said of a person, inscribed when they are dead, not something you would never say

explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is an inscription on a tomb, the final words about the dead.

clue.text: Recovery in motor sport

explanation.surface: A comeback in car racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallying means recovering strength or prices; it is also competitive road driving over a set route.

clue.text: Fireman Bram

explanation.surface: A firefighter whose name is Bram.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoker feeds a furnace, a fireman on a steam engine; Bram Stoker wrote Dracula.
